A.notes:
All sections looks good.
On the activity charts page, I don't think an accordion is t he right choice for the categories list. Also, the "about these charts" section is in an accordion at the bottom which will make it hard for users to find when many categories are listed. That is not the right choice. A tooltip would be better.

B.notes:
The vertical spacing between text and content is too large and pushes the main content down too far. It also makes it harder to see the bottom note starting with "submissions compare the last..." as a footnote, because it is not using proximity effectively. 

On the activity charts page, this build used a modal for the categories list, thats great! The button affordance icon makes me think it will open a list or dropdown, and that was a little bit confusing as a user. 

This build also used a sort bar, great! The categories button and the sort bar have too close a proximity which makes it harder to tell that they are distinct affordances. Sort could have been floated right on the same row and that would have helped. 

The small 'i' icon for the about these charts info is too subtle. Many users would miss it.

C.notes:
All sections looks good. This is the first build that I can remember used a pill shape for the category inside the card. I think it works. 

On the activity charts page, I think the categories affordance is working well. The list icon is harmonious with the smaller tooltip that opens (not a full page modal) and it is not unexpected like it was in Build b. But again it has too much proximity to the sort bar. Floating one element left and the other right in the same row is probably all that is needed.

The "about these charts" section is in an accordion at the bottom which will make it hard for users to find when many categories are listed. That is not the right choice. A tooltip would be better.

D.notes:
I like that this build put the "needs attention" lozenge/alert higher up in the card. None of the other builds have done that. It makes it easier to pay attention to it. Even better would be if it was floated right in the top corner so it did not push the other content down and disrupt the horizontal alignment across cards. 

On the activity charts page, the text content and sort bar are too close vertically. More elegant use of proximity would make it easier to user this page.

together: These were the most successful builds yet. Several builds used tooltips or modals for the categories list and 'about these charts' link, so the updates to the docs did work for some of the agents. Logical and elegant use of proximity seems to still be a challenge.
picks_note: Picked in chat on 2026-10-14: the review page ran an older runner (another session had switched the branch), so it asked for verdicts, all 'changes'. Shamsi: 'Builds C and D both did pretty well. I choose D because C forgot the footer.'
